source.title: Super Tiny Language Models
source.authors: Dylan Hillier; Leon Guertler; Cheston Tan; Palaash Agrawal; Rui-Rui Chen; Bobby Cheng

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure 1 is referenced, but its plotted values are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own architecture comparisons and validation-perplexity and benchmark outcomes. These bear narrowly on architecture sensitivity and downstream predictability, but it does not run the original scaling-law sweeps.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling laws as background and mentions Kaplan et al. as motivation for changing datasets; it does not sweep parameter count, training tokens, or compute, fit scaling laws, or test compute-optimal allocation. Its own relevant results are baseline comparisons around 50M parameters. The authors state qualitative validation-perplexity comparisons for Simple FFN and DropoutFree; Figure 1 is cited but its numeric curves are unavailable here. Table 2 also reports benchmark scores for these variants.
record.test_reason: An introductory position paper. Its only experiments are a few ~50M-parameter baselines that vary positional embedding, FFN type and dropout. There is no sweep of parameters, tokens or compute and no fitted law. Kaplan et al. is used only to justify moving to a larger dataset. Perplexity comparisons are qualitative (Figure 1 values unavailable). The benchmark scores sit near chance and differ by at most about 1–4 points, so they cannot show whether loss differences are slight (V4) or whether downstream performance tracks loss or scale (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The paper is an introductory vision paper, and its baselines are preliminary. It does tentatively say the results reinforce the value of RoPE, and that Simple FFN does incrementally better despite higher perplexity, but needs validation because of the FFN-dimension confound. It draws no conclusion about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a small set of roughly 50M-parameter architecture baselines rather than fitting loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute scaling curves or testing compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and dropout setting are varied; the authors specifically note that the Simple FFN dimension differs from the baseline and complicates interpretation.

fits_no_version.finding: At ~50M parameters, Simple FFN has higher validation perplexity than the baseline but equal or 1-point-higher zero-shot scores. DropoutFree has lower perplexity with comparable scores. The authors flag the Simple FFN FFN-dimension confound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Among same-size architecture variants of tiny LMs, small validation-perplexity differences do not order zero-shot benchmark accuracy, which sits near chance.

record.problems: The relevant runs are a small set near 50M parameters, with no reported uncertainty or repeated-run results. Validation-perplexity differences are qualitative in the text and the referenced figure's numeric curves are unavailable. The Simple FFN comparison changes FFN dimension, which the authors identify as a confound.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 scores for other architecture variants are not included because the text does not connect their benchmark results to an explicit validation-perplexity result. Scores for external models in Table 2 are comparisons, not results from this study's own experiments. Figure 1 is referenced but has no recoverable plotted values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No sweep of parameters, tokens or compute.
No depth/width variation at fixed size; perplexity differences between variants not quantified.
No scale sweep or loss-to-downstream mapping; benchmarks near chance.

record.verdict_notes: Kaplan et al. is invoked only to argue that a ~50M model needs about 1B words to avoid overfitting, which motivated the switch to OpenWebText. The reader's V4 and V6 'tested' statuses and limits_scope labels are not supported: no scale is varied and no loss magnitudes are given.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of parameters, tokens, or compute; no test of loss power laws.
No fits on small runs or predictions for larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation experiment or parameter/token scaling with compute.
Only a few architecture variants near 50M parameters are compared; the experiments do not cover a wide range of depths, widths, or parameter counts, and numeric loss differences are not stated.
No results for other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No systematic scale sweep or quantitative mapping from held-out loss to downstream performance; only selected near-50M architecture comparisons and listed benchmark scores are reported.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, training schedules, or scaling-law exponents.
